extracted.intended_audience: third‑party requesters, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing a request for inter partes reexamination of a U.S. patent under 37 CFR 1.913–1.919 and related MPEP guidance, including required certifications, documents, service, and formatting. Covers who may file, estoppel limitations, required content, form/formatting, and filing-date consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on subsequent inter partes requests after an order (37 CFR 1.931)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an order to reexamine has been issued under §1.931, neither the third party requester, nor its privies, may file a subsequent request for inter partes reexamination of the patent until an inter partes reexamination certificate is issued under §1.997, unless authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute bar (subject only to Director authorization) to refiling by the same requester or its privies while a prior inter partes reexamination remains pending; plan timing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel after final decision in related civil action (28 U.S.C. 1338)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision has been entered against a party in a civil action under 28 U.S.C. 1338 that the party failed to prove invalidity of any patent claim-in-suit, then that party and its privies may not thereafter request inter partes reexamination of any such patent claim on the basis of issues which that party or its privies raised or could have raised in such civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request based on issues previously litigated and decided adversely will be barred and may not be maintained by the Office; assess prior litigation outcomes before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel after favorable final decision in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision in an inter partes reexamination instituted by a third party requester is favorable to patentability of any original, proposed amended, or new claims of the patent, then that party and its privies may not thereafter request inter partes reexamination of any such patent claims on the basis of issues which that party or its privies raised or could have raised in that proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester who obtains a favorable final decision on patentability is estopped from re-raising the same issues in a later inter partes request; evaluate possible estoppel consequences of pursuing reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a request (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in 37 CFR 1.907, any person other than the patent owner may file a request for inter partes reexamination of a patent (37 CFR 1.913). The patent owner is precluded from initiating inter partes reexamination of its patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should use ex parte reexamination or reissue instead. Typical non-owner filers include licensees, potential licensees, infringers, ITC respondents, interference applicants, and litigants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel/prohibition certification and limits on USPTO inquiry (37 CFR 1.915(b)(7) & 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.915(b)(7) requires the third party requester to certify that the estoppel provisions of 37 CFR 1.907 do not prohibit the inter partes reexamination. That certification constitutes a prima facie showing that the party requesting reexamination is not barred; the Office generally will not look beyond this certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner may challenge the certification, but the challenger must facially establish that the requester is barred. The Office lacks subpoena/discovery/hearing authority to investigate real-party-in-interest disputes; courts are the appropriate forum for detailed factual inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the real party in interest (37 CFR 1.915(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a statement identifying the real party in interest to the extent necessary for a subsequent person filing an inter partes reexamination request to determine whether that person is a privy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient identification so future requesters can determine privy status; this information is relied upon for later estoppel/privity certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney/agent authority and representation requirements (37 CFR 1.915(c), 1.34, 1.32(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is filed by an attorney or agent identifying another party on whose behalf the request is filed, the attorney or agent must have a power of attorney from that party or be acting in a representative capacity pursuant to §1.34. A power of attorney may only name as representative the inventors or registered patent practitioners (37 CFR 1.32(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney/agent acting in representative capacity must set forth registration number, name, and signature. The representative must be a registered patent practitioner. Proof of authority may be required if questioned. During reexamination, a third party requester may not be represented by a person not registered to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for requesting inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.915(a) and 1.20(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be accompanied by the fee for requesting inter partes reexamination set forth in §1.20(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include the fee will generally trigger notice and an opportunity to complete; omission may prevent granting of a filing date. Note: because patent owners may not file inter partes requests, excess-claims fees at filing are not an issue for inter partes requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of patent and every claim for which reexamination is requested (37 CFR 1.915(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify the patent by patent number and every claim for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not required, it is strongly suggested to also state the patentee and patent title to prevent mis-typing errors in the patent number. Clearly identify each claim the requester wants reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of patents and printed publications presenting a substantial new question (37 CFR 1.915(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include a citation of the patents and printed publications which are presented to provide a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form PTO/SB/08A or 08B or PTO/SB/42 (or an equivalent format) to list all cited patents and printed publications. The art cited by a requester must be comprehensively listed to assist the examiner and to meet statutory mandates for special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement pointing out each substantial new question and detailed explanation of pertinency (37 CFR 1.915(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must contain a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on the cited patents and printed publications, and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the patents and printed publications to every claim for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must identify each substantial new question of patentability and each proposed ground of rejection separately. For each identified question/ground, explain how the cited documents are applied to meet or teach the patent claim limitations to establish the substantial new question or proposed ground. The request must apply all cited prior art to the claims requested for reexamination. See MPEP §§2616–2617 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of every patent/printed publication and required translations (37 CFR 1.915(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to in paragraphs (b)(1)–(3) must be provided, accompanied by an English language translation of all necessary and pertinent parts of any non-English document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full copies so the examiner can fully consider each reference. At minimum, translate the portions relied upon. Provide the listing of patents/printed publications as required by 37 CFR 1.98; comprehensive listing is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of entire patent and related documents; formatting (37 CFR 1.915(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a copy of the entire patent including the front face, drawings, and specification/claims (in double column format) for which reexamination is requested, and a copy of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent. All copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the printed patent reproduced on one side of paper in double-column format; present drawing pages and front page as in the printed patent. Include prior disclaimers/certificates as part of the patent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service on the patent owner (37 CFR 1.915(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a certification by the third party requester that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided for in §1.33(c), and must indicate the name and address of the party served. If service was not possible, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service could not be effected after reasonable effort, provide a duplicate copy to the Office along with a cover letter explaining efforts made and why service failed. To avoid erroneous duplicate-filing fees, clearly label the cover letter (e.g., “Duplicate Copy of Request Filed under 37 CFR 1.915(b)(6) When Service on the Patent Owner Was Not Possible”).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for incomplete requests and filing-date rule (37 CFR 1.919(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a request for inter partes reexamination is the date on which the request satisfies all the requirements in §1.915. Requests that fail to satisfy all requirements are incomplete and will not be granted a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a reexamination filing date, include the fee and satisfy all §1.915 requirements. Incomplete requests may be placed in the patent file merely as a citation (per §1.501). An application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 cannot be submitted in a reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/58 (transmittal/cover sheet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/58 is encouraged for use as the transmittal form and cover sheet of a request for inter partes reexamination, but its use is not required by law or rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/58 provides an organized checklist (fee payment, identification of requester and real party in interest, list of cited art, copies enclosed, claims identified, service certification, concurrent proceedings, correspondence address, signature). Using the form helps ensure completeness but is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness recommendation — include all relevant art and explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The request should be as complete as possible, since there is no guarantee the examiner will consider other art when deciding on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all patents/printed publications and detailed claim charts/explanations you want the examiner to consider; omission risks that the examiner will not consider omitted references in deciding whether a substantial new question exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and forwarding instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence for a third party requester is addressed to the requester, unless a specific indication is made to forward correspondence to another address (e.g., a representative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly designate the preferred correspondence address (customer number or firm/individual contact). If correspondence should be sent to a representative, explicitly indicate forwarding instructions on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical users of inter partes reexamination (who commonly files)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons likely to use inter partes reexamination include licensees, potential licensees, infringers, potential exporters, patent litigants, interference applicants, and International Trade Commission respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list helps potential requesters evaluate whether inter partes is the appropriate proceeding for their factual or litigation posture; it is informational rather than a filing requirement.
